repairVerification.finding: V5-B1 (raised by BOTH reviewers) - the no-lock-until-DR-111 rule conflicted with still-required lock fixtures
repairVerification.howIChecked: I re-scanned every string in the whole document for 'lock' and classified each hit. TC-SIG/requires dropped from 3 members to 2: 'artifact bytes vs lock digest mismatch' is removed and re-enters at TC-SIG/conditionalRequires gated on DR-111 with the scoped-disposition clause the class already uses for ENVELOPE_MISMATCH. TC-BYTE-EXACT/requires[0] now reads 'a fixture whose admission digest and index custody digest recompute from stored bytes (no lock digest until DR-111)', preserving the two halves that are producible today, and its scopeNote adds the DR-111 gate for the lock-digest half. No remaining string anywhere in v6 requires a lock fixture unconditionally.
repairVerification.residual: None blocking. See advisory V6-A2 on the three different gate expressions.

I re-measured all of them myself with hashlib rather than trusting the record: SRC-08 live 1cdcf9d4071a6c5eaa7cd7d28fac288eaced796c9ee906b6f1db0f7a4b1f95b3, SRC-D live 12d192f758f48f692e69cb410a1d7a9bf776c765257c8e910272d3de457ec3e3, SRC-FRZ live e809d4395f394a507c36c23c069d566c838b2283c931b6d2d13797be53406dbd - all three exactly as v6 records them. SRC-02 1811c682... and SRC-03 52158469... still match their v2 pins, as v6 states. The v5 repairLog entry V4-S2 is left byte-identical and v6's V5-B2 entry states plainly that it is historical and that the field work is completed under V5-S1 - which is the correct handling of my finding rather than a rewrite of landed bytes.
repairVerification.residual: None blocking. See advisories V6-A4 and V6-A5 on two wording residues the rename did not reach.

repairVerification.howIChecked: Four sites moved together. lockSchema.fields[resolved].type now carries scope: 'project'|'global' in the tuple. lockSchema.fields[resolved].semantics states 'The custody join to the index is by (stableId, version, scope), matching entryShape and shadowedBy.' The ordering rule at resolutionInputs.semantics is now (stableId, version, scope). lockSchema.purpose describes the tuples as (stableId, provenance, version, scope, digest). entryShape.stableId and shadowedBy are byte-identical to v5, so the index side of the join is unmoved and the two sides now agree.

repairVerification.howIChecked: purpose now carries 'NO lock is producible until DR-111 closes; this field describes the deferred record, not a presently producible artifact.' The SRC-03 owning sentence is quoted verbatim and unchanged around it.

repairVerification.finding: V5-A3 - the dual-scope exclusion was not provenance-qualified while the multi-version exclusion was
repairVerification.howIChecked: Both sites moved. collisionUniverse now excludes 'same-(stableId, provenance, version) dual-scope admission' and adds the decisive gloss 'a different-provenance claimant at the same stableId is RJ-1 regardless of scope'. RJ-2's trigger carries the matching text. The exclusion is now symmetric with the multi-version arm, and the asymmetry I flagged is closed at the level of the rule rather than left to RJ-1 as a backstop.

repairVerification.finding: V5-A4 - collisionUniverse's shadowedBy phrasing ('plus version') was stale
repairVerification.howIChecked: Now reads 'which is also how shadowedBy - the same triple - identifies a unique entry', matching entryShape.shadowedBy's (stableId, version, scope).

repairVerification.finding: V5-A5 - RJ-2's DIFFERENT-(stableId, provenance) qualifier attached only to the last enumerated item
repairVerification.howIChecked: The trigger is re-punctuated into three explicit branches: 'against the reserved list (unconditional); against live names/aliases and live entries' MOUNTED ROOT COMMAND NAMES of a DIFFERENT (stableId, provenance); or within the manifest's own command tree'. The qualifier now unambiguously covers live names/aliases as well as mounted roots, and the reserved arm is explicitly unconditional.

advisories.title: RJ-4's lock-digest trigger arm is dormant until DR-111 and carries no marker, although the same rule already uses a conditional marker for its other deferred arm
advisories.detail: RJ-4's trigger still reads '...artifact bytes not matching a lock/index-recorded digest.' With no lock producible until DR-111, the lock half of that clause cannot fire; the index-recorded half remains fully reachable, so the rule is not broken. RJ-4 already models deferral explicitly via conditionalSubcode for ENVELOPE_MISMATCH, and TC-SIG's fixture side was moved to conditionalRequires in this very revision, so the artifact has two conventions available and applied neither to this clause. A half-sentence noting that the lock arm activates with DR-111 would make the refusal surface and the corpus surface say the same thing.
advisories.notABlocker: No behaviour is authorized that the deferral forbids, and the fixture obligation is correctly gated at TC-SIG.

advisories.title: The same DR-111 lock gate is expressed three different ways across three classes
advisories.detail: TC-ACCEPT keeps its lock member inside requires[5] with inline deferral prose ('...is a required class member DEFERRED until DR-111; no lock fixture is required or producible until then'). TC-SIG moves its lock member out of requires into conditionalRequires. TC-BYTE-EXACT edits the lock clause out of requires[0] and states the gate in scopeNote. All three say the same thing and none is wrong - and because every requires member is prose rather than a machine token, no tool can mis-enumerate them. But a reader comparing classes sees one deferred member still sitting in a requires array while an identically deferred member was moved out of another. Normalizing on conditionalRequires would remove the asymmetry that produced V5-B1 in the first place.
advisories.notABlocker: Each expression is individually unambiguous and self-contained; I verified no class requires a lock fixture unconditionally.

advisories.title: TC-SIG.conditionalRequires now carries two independently gated members concatenated in one prose string
advisories.detail: The field holds the ENVELOPE_MISMATCH member (gated on ID-DEP-1 and ID-DEP-5) and, after an 'ALSO:', the lock-digest-mismatch member (gated on DR-111). requires is an array; conditionalRequires is a single string, so two members with different gates now share one value and must be separated by reading the prose. Making conditionalRequires an array of {member, gate} would match how requires is already shaped.
advisories.notABlocker: Both gates are stated correctly and each names its own owning surface and scoped-disposition terms.

advisories.title: SRC-PROTO's 'this authoring' wording was not scoped alongside the measuredAtV2Authoring rename
advisories.detail: Codex V5-S1's finding text named SRC-PROTO alongside the measuredAtAuthoring flags. The v6 repair operation is scoped to '/sources/bindingSources/*/measuredAtAuthoring', a field SRC-PROTO does not have, so SRC-PROTO still reads verifiedAtAuthoring 'git rev-parse HEAD returned exactly this commit; working tree clean at measurement time' and custodyCaveats '...the pin is re-verified at each measurement time (it was, this authoring)'. In a v6 document 'this authoring' reads as a v6 claim that reMeasurementAtV6 does not record. I checked the substance independently rather than assume it stale: the prototype repository HEAD is exactly a62509d623173155d0946e9f5d5ca90c839893e0 and git status --porcelain is empty. The claim is therefore TRUE as measured at this review, which is why this is an advisory on wording scope and not a custody finding.
advisories.notABlocker: The pin verifies clean. Unlike the whole-document pins that motivated V5-B2, nothing here is false.

advisories.title: corpusHeadAtAuthoring keeps a bare 'AtAuthoring' name whose v2 scoping lives only in a historical note
advisories.detail: /sources/corpusHeadAtAuthoring is d31df3866157d4edaa316a371128c83eef43f2f5, the v2 authoring head (live HEAD at this review is 2327cf89106e3c58a317bf8b570697f3505dbbb8). Its v2 scoping is stated in reMeasurementAtV5 - retained, but a predecessor's note - while v6's own reMeasurementAtV6 scopes only the bindingSources digests. The bindingSources flags got renamed to measuredAtV2Authoring in this revision; this sibling field did not. Same one-word treatment would close it.
advisories.notABlocker: reMeasurementAtV2 and reMeasurementAtV5 are both retained in the document, so the v2 scoping is recoverable on the artifact's own bytes.

Codex v5 carries exactly blockers [V5-B1], shouldFix [V5-S1], advisories [V5-A1]; v6's codexV5 record states precisely that, and the three repairLog verdictTitles reproduce Codex's titles. The id-collision note is accurate on both counts: my V5-S1 (open-ended method roster) is not Codex's V5-S1 (custody flags), and my V5-A1 (lockSchema.purpose) is not Codex's V5-A1 (basedOn.method hedge); the repairLog correctly disambiguates those two as CLAUDE-V5-S1 and CLAUDE-V5-A1 while leaving my non-colliding ids unprefixed.
